# Reverting a tell kills the user with a new entry - the log only ever grows.
# Reverting that revert tells them again, with the key material on record.

env GIT_EDITOR=true
sesam-repo admin
exec sesam hook install

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'tell bob'

# A dry run plans the inverse and touches nothing.
exec sesam revert --dry-run HEAD
stdout '^- user bob$'
exec git status --porcelain
! stdout .

# A plain git revert of HEAD runs no driver and no pre-commit. The
# prepare-commit-msg hook catches the truncated log and points to sesam revert.
! exec git revert --no-edit HEAD
stderr 'drops entries that HEAD holds'
stderr 'git reset --merge., then .sesam revert [0-9a-f]+'
exec git reset --merge
exec git log --oneline
! stdout 'Revert'

exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^- user bob$'
stderr 'git revert --continue'
exec git revert --continue
exec git log -1 --format=%s
stdout 'Revert "tell bob"'

exec sesam user list
! stdout bob
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"user.kill"'
exec sesam verify --all
! stderr 'not a prefix'

# Reverting the revert brings bob back.
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^\+ user bob \(groups: dev\)$'
exec git revert --continue
exec sesam user list
stdout bob
exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"user.tell"'
exec sesam verify --all
! stderr 'not a prefix'
